name: INNIO

logo.source: innio.com site header logo (https://www.innio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/innio_logo_black.svg); no Wikipedia page or Commons SVG for INNIO N.V.

description: INNIO makes the reciprocating gas engines (Jenbacher and Waukesha brands) that turn natural, renewable and specialty gases into electricity, heat or pipeline compression, and then earns a long tail of parts and service on the installed base of about 44 GW. About half of revenue is one-time equipment sales (new engines and gensets) and about half is services; the services line is the higher-margin one. Since 2025 the equipment side has been swamped by AI data-center orders for behind-the-meter power: data-center equipment revenue went from about 5% of Q3 2025 revenue to about 40% of Q3 2026 revenue, and one energy-as-a-service customer (VoltaGrid) was about 41% of 2025 equipment order intake. Remaining performance obligations were $10.9 billion at 2026-09-30. It is controlled by Advent and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority through its principal shareholder, which sold the 103.5 million IPO shares itself, so INNIO received no IPO proceeds.

hq.note: Cover page lists Nymphenburger Strasse 5, Munich and a US address at 1101 W. St. Paul Ave., Waukesha, Wisconsin. Netherlands-incorporated holding company (N.V.). Main production hubs are in Austria (Jenbach, Hall, Kapfenberg) and North America (Welland, Waukesha, Waller, Trenton).

employees.note: Full-time equivalents in 22 countries (Q3 2026 10-Q). 5,202 FTEs at 2026-03-31 (prospectus).

businessLines.name: Equipment (new engines, gensets and project equipment)
businessLines.how: One-time sale of engines, gensets and containerized power packages, sold directly to hyperscalers, colocation operators and utilities or through distributors and packagers; revenue follows large project orders and delivery timing.
businessLines.description: Designs, manufactures and sells new Jenbacher and Waukesha engines, project-related equipment and related solutions to data center, power solutions and compression markets.

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Segment EBITDA (company's non-GAAP segment profit measure, not operating income); FY2024 $120.6M. Q3 2026: $132.8M vs $65.7M; nine months 2026: $234.4M.

businessLines.name: Services (aftermarket parts and service)
businessLines.how: Recurring sales of parts and labor on engines the company already installed; some customers sign long-term agreements (up to ten years or more, billed on operating hours), others buy parts and overhauls as needed; through distributors it often sells parts only.
businessLines.description: Lifecycle services on the installed base: spare parts, overhauls, remanufacturing, conversions, modifications and upgrades, long-term service agreements, and digital services (myplant, about 13,000 connected engines and assets).

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Segment EBITDA (non-GAAP segment profit measure); FY2024 $373.5M. Q3 2026: $123.7M vs $90.1M; nine months 2026: $343.4M.

brands.name: Waukesha
brands.segment: Equipment and Services (US-built gas engines, strong in compression)

brands.name: myplant
brands.share: About 13,000 connected engines and assets; revenue not separately reported
